subject: Inference thresholds, model fit, and deployment commitments (AtlasRx)
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Stern <alex.stern@atlasrx.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Inference thresholds, model fit, and deployment commitments (AtlasRx)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick write-up of what we heard, open items, and next steps so we all have the same frame.

Summary of pain points / context
- User-facing chat product: median response quality OK but tail latencies and burst costs are blocking launch.
- Current hosted model (closed provider) is expensive at scale; procurement wants predictable unit economics.
- Peak concurrency during reports: sustained ~600 qps for 30–45min + occasional spikes to ~1.2k qps.

Primary goals
1) 99th-percentile end-to-end (client -> token stream start) < 300ms for typical 64-token replies; streaming chunk latency target < 150ms.
2) Throughput profile: support 600 sustained qps with headroom for 2x burst.
3) Cost target: reduce per-1000-token cost by >= 3x compared to current provider (ballpark target provided on call).
4) Data controls: PHI in some flows — requirement for private deployment option or strong VPC/KMS controls.

Technical notes we captured
- Preferred model family: open/quantizable models (Llama2-13B/13B-chat or similar). Need to validate accuracy vs current model.
- Kernel & quantization: plan to test 4-bit/8-bit post-training quantization and evaluate NVMe-backed KV caching for long conversations.
- Batching: continuous/latency-aware batching required to hit throughput targets while honoring streaming SLOs.
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to a smaller model variant during bursts to preserve availability.
- Observability: token-level latency and cost traces required for each route/model.

Topology options discussed
A) Hosted Redwood API with reserved Dedicated pools for production traffic (fastest time-to-market).
B) Dedicated capacity (customer-dedicated GPU pools) with private networking for PHI-sensitive flows.
C) Hybrid: host non-PHI in Redwood hosted; route PHI to Private (VPC) deployment with same control-plane.

Immediate next steps / owners (proposed)
- Redwood (David): topology sketch + rough TCO by Fri 23 Jul (attachment: latency-slo-table.csv).
- AtlasRx (Alex): share 3 sample conversation logs (anonymized) and typical prompt lengths by Tue 20 Jul.
- Redwood (Marissa): run model-fit evaluation (Llama2-13B 4-bit vs 8-bit) and share initial quality delta by Mon 26 Jul.
- AtlasRx (Priya): procurement checklist & SOC2 evidence request attached — procurement will confirm required artifacts.

Attachments: atlasrx-mpa-draft.docx (mutual action plan template), latency-slo-table.csv (estimates).

If this matches your view, we can lock the technical deep-dive for July 27 (45min) to walk topology sketches and run-cards.

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.inference/docs
From: Alex Stern <alex.stern@atlasrx.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference thresholds, model fit, and deployment commitments (AtlasRx)

Thanks David — this is great and aligns with our notes. Two quick clarifications before the deep-dive: 

1) Tokenization / prompt templates: the client concatenates a fixed header (~35 tokens) + user message (avg 48 tokens, 95th percentile 220 tokens). We will upload anonymized examples. Will that affect your batching recommendations?

2) Streaming: we stream partial tokens to the UI. Does Redwood measure the streaming chunk start latency (i.e., first-byte-to-client) or just backend generation latency? We want streaming experience to feel instantaneous.

Also +1 on July 27 — Alex and I will attend. Adding procurement on follow-up.

Best,
Alex
Alex Stern | VP Product, AtlasRx
alex.stern@atlasrx.com
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Stern <alex.stern@atlasrx.com>, Priya Rao <priya@atlasrx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference thresholds, model fit, and deployment commitments (AtlasRx)

Great questions Alex — short answers below and a few clarifications.

- Prompt length: large variance (95th 220 tokens) implies batching window needs to be size-aware; we'll propose per-route batching profiles (small-window for short prompts, larger-window for non-streaming bulk).
- Streaming measurement: Redwood can report both (a) backend generation latency (token emit downstream) and (b) first-byte-to-client streaming latency. For your UX target, we'll track chunk-first-byte < 150ms as an SLO.
- Model fallback: plan to have an explicitly pinned small-variant (e.g., 7B quantized) for burst routing; real-time routing decisions based on queue depth and token backlog.

Action: Marissa, Rishi — can you validate model-fit evaluation plan and feed baseline accuracy metrics from our eval harness? We'll need rough timeline in the topology sketch.

David

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: AtlasRx — quick internal action items (model-fit, kernels, cost)

Team — summarizing internal owner list and asks following Alex's clarifying questions. Keep this thread for traceability.

1) Model-fit eval (Marissa) — run Llama2-13B 8-bit and 4-bit evals against AtlasRx-provided prompts once they arrive. Deliverable: quality delta report + latency wall-clock (P50/P95/P99) for single-request generation. Due: Mon 26 Jul.
2) Kernel selection & quant perf (Jasmine) — run kernel mix tests (cuBLAS/cuDNN + Triton fallback; if using AMD, note kernel parity). Provide expected NVMe KV cache impact on P99 for long histories. Deliverable: perf matrix and recommended kernel config. Due: Tue 27 Jul (to include in topology sketch).
3) Topology & TCO sketch (Rishi + David) — produce cost-per-1000-token estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Hybrid (assume 600 sustained qps, 2x burst). Include SLO tradeoffs (streaming chunk-first-byte <150ms) and fallback costs. Due: Fri 23 Jul.

I'll assemble these into the topology sketch and share with AtlasRx ahead of the 27 Jul deep-dive. If you need infra access or sample logs to validate numbers, ping Alex for upload link.

Thanks —
David

- For PHI flows we will need key-management detail (KMS/HSM) and audit-log retention windows.

We'll share anonymized conversation logs today (upload in the Drive link you provided). Confirming Alex + I will attend the Jul 27 deep-dive.

Regards,
